definition: to destroy a large part of something
hook: Decimate is a math problem, and the answer is one in ten.
modernAnchor: A storm flattens a town. A recession wipes out a market. We say it was decimated.
journey: Latin decem meant ten, and decimare meant to take a tenth.
When a Roman legion mutinied or fled, the army answered with a brutal punishment.
The soldiers were split into groups of ten and drew lots. The one who drew the short lot was beaten to death by the other nine.
Over the centuries the exact fraction faded, and decimate came to mean destroying almost anything on a large scale.
